A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSR research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations and experiments on CartPole, CoinRun and five Atari games, including performance comparisons, ablations and reconstruction analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds prediction-error and adaptation-mode diagnostics in Appendix D.4 and Figure 14.

M1.justification: Section 3 changes the reward contribution in the stated reconstruction objective from p_phi(r_t | ...) to log p_phi(r_t | ...). This is a limited loss-formula correction; the three-step CSR framework remains intact. Expanded pseudocode chiefly documents existing operations and does not establish that the implementation or experiments changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same simulated environments, CartPole variations, CoinRun difficulty transfer and five Atari games. The added Pong diagnostic uses modes and difficulties already covered; no new dataset, domain or task requirement is introduced.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: DQN, Dreamer and AdaRL in simulation, CartPole and CoinRun; Random, SPR, Dreamer, AdaRL and EfficientZero in Table 2. The expansion-strategy comparison also retains Random, Deterministic and Self-Adaptive.

E3.justification: The added Appendix D.4 diagnostic specifies a controlled Pong sequence of (mode, difficulty) pairs: (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0), and measures prediction errors and adaptation-mode selections. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged. Newly disclosed detection-step budgets belong to implementation documentation and do not establish revised budgets.

E4.justification: Figure 14 and Appendix D.4 add a focused analysis of whether prediction error and the selected adaptation mechanism correspond to environmental changes across the four environment families. Existing causal-structure ablations, expansion-strategy comparisons and latent-variable removal analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over five runs and retain the same tabulated uncertainty values and shaded learning curves. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: The added Figure 14 reports new diagnostic results, including Pong prediction errors of 0.2, 0.15, 1.77 and 0.09 across its four tasks, plus adaptation-mode selections. Existing performance and expansion results in Tables 1–3 and retained learning curves are unchanged; these additions do not show improved benchmark performance over v3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the reconstruction objective in Section 3 is corrected by inserting a logarithm on the reward probability. The identifiability definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–3, Proposition 1, Corollary 1 and Appendix A proofs otherwise remain unchanged apart from notation and equation numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: adaptation to distribution shifts and space expansions through causal representations and a three-step strategy, with efficient transfer and superior reported performance. Revised captions and question-based experiment headings emphasize existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 newly interprets the diagnostics as supporting prediction error's reliability for selecting adaptation mechanisms. Appendices C and E add prospective applications involving other policy learners, goal misalignment and continual or domain-agnostic RL. Existing nonstationarity and nonlinear-identifiability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation expands substantially: Algorithm 1 details initialization, parameter updates, policy learning and environment interaction; new Appendix D.1 specifies network components, mask approximations, gradients, optimizer and environment-specific detection budgets. Section 4 adds a code-access link. Existing hyperparameter tables and hardware/time disclosures are retained; the PDFs do not establish changed implementations or verify the linked resource.

R1.justification: v4 adds implementation and future-direction references, including Ng et al. (2022), Di Langosco et al. (2022) and Khetarpal et al. (2022), and removes the Hafner et al. (2019) reference. Section 5 and the principal positioning against methods assuming fixed environment spaces remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 is reframed around three explicit questions, introductory environment descriptions move to Appendix D.3, and the appendices gain clearer subdivisions and a future-directions section. Local wording, affiliations, publication headers and acknowledgments also change. Most main-text prose and its section order are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the causal-graph illustration in Figure 5 and diagnostic plots in Figure 14, expands and reformats Algorithm 1, and adds highlighting to the reconstruction comparison now numbered Figure 13. Captions gain emphasized takeaways, and appendix displays move. Existing benchmark plots and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the paper through more actionable implementation documentation, a corrected reconstruction objective, clearer explanations and direct diagnostic evidence for adaptation decisions in Figure 14. These targeted gains strengthen clarity and reproducibility. The central performance evidence and identifiability arguments remain unchanged, while the newly discussed broader applications remain prospective.
